payload.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=stability+of+interaction-induced+attractor+states+in+recurrent+human-AI+feedback+loops+dynamical+systems+theory&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7194881\", \"title\": [\"From Feedback Loops to Spectra: Stability of the Interaction Matrix in Rock Engineering Systems\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>In Rock Engineering Systems (RES), the interacting factors of a problem are arranged in an interaction matrix, and the fully coupled model of Jiao and Hudson turns that matrix into a global description in which every factor can act on every other through chains and feedback loops. This is meaningful only if the feedback settles rather than grows without bound. Earlier work tested that loop by loop, requiring each feedback loop, or loops meeting at a common variable, to stay below a critical strength; such tests are only approximate, and where loops share no variable they can accept an unstable system or reject a stable one. This paper instead gives a spectral and pseudospectral treatment of the rock engineering interaction matrix, drawing on recent developments in non-normal matrix analysis and robust-stability theory from numerical linear algebra. The global interaction matrix is the resolvent (I - A)⁻¹ of the interaction matrix A, and the coupled system is stable exactly when the spectral radius ρ(A), the largest eigenvalue magnitude, is below one. Two margins measure how far a stable system sits from instability: a multiplicative margin independent of the variables&apos; units, and a pseudospectral margin that reveals the non-normality the eigenvalues conceal. Closed-form expressions rank the mechanisms that most move the stability boundary. The framework is demonstrated on Jiao and Hudson&apos;s six-variable dam foundation and nine-variable hydroelectric pressure tunnel, reproducing their published global matrices, and it extends to larger multi-domain systems.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7194881\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1142/s0218339095000381\", \"title\": [\"FEEDBACK LOOPS, STABILITY AND MULTISTATIONARITY IN DYNAMICAL SYSTEMS\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p> By fairly simple considerations of stability and multistationarity in nonlinear systems of first order differential equations it is shown that under quite mild restrictions a negative feedback loop is a necessary condition for stability, and that a positive feedback loop is a necessary condition for multistationarity. </jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1142/s0218339095000381\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[1995, 6]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1017/s0143385710000878\", \"title\": [\"Structural stability of attractor–repellor endomorphisms with singularities\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>We prove a theorem on the structural stability of smooth attractor–repellor endomorphisms of compact manifolds, with singularities. By attractor–repellor, we mean that the non-wandering set of the dynamics <jats:italic>f</jats:italic> is the disjoint union of an expanding compact subset with a hyperbolic attractor on which <jats:italic>f</jats:italic> acts bijectively. The statement of this result is both infinitesimal and dynamical. To our knowledge, this is the first in this hybrid direction. Our results also generalize Mather’s theorem in singularity theory, which states that infinitesimal stability implies structural stability for composed mappings to the larger category of laminations.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1017/s0143385710000878\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2011, 6, 10]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6308121\", \"title\": [\"Claude’s Law: Quantifying Super-Exponential Growth in AI Capability Through Interaction-Scale Feedback Loops\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Moore's Law has governed hardware capability growth for five decades: processing power doubles approximately every 18 months. However, recent observations suggest that AI software capability is improving at a significantly faster rate. This paper proposes \\\"Claude's Law\\\" as a framework for understanding this acceleration: AI improvement scales with the product of multiple exponentially growing factors-human access, application proliferation, deployment depth, interaction frequency, and feedback incorporation efficiency-creating super-exponential growth when these factors compound.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6308121\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "8c5427ec24cd1fc891dfdcb33f3f5081103bd0f373bc694e0938418439cd7d25", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "emergent_preferences", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.2139/ssrn.7194881", "doi:10.1142/s0218339095000381", "doi:10.1017/s0143385710000878", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.6308121"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7194881", "https://doi.org/10.1142/s0218339095000381", "https://doi.org/10.1017/s0143385710000878", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.6308121"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
